The watcher\\u0027s ExecuteAsync is a do-while that polls once synchronously inside StartAsync (BackgroundService calls ExecuteAsync on the caller\\u0027s thread) and then every 250 ms on a PeriodicTimer. So the first poll always happens before the delay begins, and the race only bites when that first poll fails transiently and no retry completes before StopAsync cancels the loop. The likely transient is inferred, not observed (the move\\u0027s catch is silent and the tests use NullLogger): IsOwnStopRequest claims the request by File.Move and swallows an IOException from a sharing violation (a scanner or indexer holding the just-written file open, common on windows-latest), returning false for the next tick to retry. In attempt 1 the file was still at the request path at assertion time, so the move itself never succeeded during the loop\\u0027s life. Both logs show heavy concurrent load at the failure (dotnet publish tests at 12 to 17 s, GitLedger tests at 14 to 15 s), and every watcher-loop test ran seconds longer than its 600 ms delay. The mechanism of that load is test-only: the watcher\\u0027s awaits carry no ConfigureAwait(false) and StartAsync is called from inside the test, so every tick continuation posts onto xUnit\\u0027s concurrency-capped synchronization context and competes for the same worker slots as every other test, including those blocking on child processes; the production host has no synchronization context. The path plumbing is not the cause: PlatformPaths.Home honors the AsyncLocal override ScopedTestHome opens in the field initializer, and it flows into the watcher\\u0027s synchronous first poll and every timer continuation; a plumbing fault would fail deterministically and on ubuntu too. xUnit runs a class\\u0027s tests sequentially on fresh instances with fresh Guid-named homes, so no sibling leaves a .claimed file behind; the start time round-trips exactly through JSON on both sides.\\n\\nFix shape, ruled by Brian 2026-09-22: observe the outcome the test already asserts on, with an async bounded wait, the way 43cf3ed7 did for the shutdown-mid-gate test; do not add a per-poll signal to the production watcher. For the ignored cases wait until both the request file and its .claimed sibling (the request path plus \\u0027.claimed\\u0027) are gone: \\u0027request file gone\\u0027 proves only the claim, and when the read after the claim fails the watcher leaves the claimed copy and decides on the next tick, so a wait on the request file alone can stop the watcher before any decision and pass both assertions vacuously. The decision follows the claimed copy\\u0027s deletion with no further I/O, and StopAsync waits the in-progress poll out before the assertions run. The bound: the existing 5 s token is linked by BackgroundService into the watcher\\u0027s stopping token, so it kills the loop too; widen that one token to 30 s and share it between StartAsync and the wait. The outcome wait returns the moment the outcome lands, faster than today\\u0027s 600 ms in the common case, so the wide bound costs nothing on the pass path. Helper shape is the build session\\u0027s call; one helper replacing RunBrieflyAsync that takes the outcome predicate and the failure words is the obvious one. 5dd55a3a\\u0027s build session (its first run ce293c59, dispatched 03:43, which later failed its host gate and was superseded) ran h9k task abandon 7af7204a with the reason \\u0027Superseded by task 5dd55a3a (idea d805fd8b, piece 4)\\u0027 and h9k idea conclude 2fa45efc, both from the worktree\\u0027s own binary. Both records replicated to the Mac and stand on both nodes. Both outcomes happened to match what Brian would have chosen (7af7204a was superseded; the idea was answered by the same merge, verified by a challenge session on 2026-09-22 08:5x), and the acceptance criteria of 5dd55a3a told the session to conclude the idea, so the session did as written. The defect is the door, not what walked through it: a dispatched session holds every lifecycle verb the owner holds, with nothing in the binary, the prompt, or the daemon stopping it from abandoning a live task or concluding an open idea. The conclusion was also recorded two hours before the removal it described had merged (06:27, #555). Brian holds this as \\u0027a dispatched session should not hold lifecycle verbs\\u0027. Pointers: a run\\u0027s worktree is identifiable from inside (the run directory and worktree layout RunPaths describes; the daemon sets the session\\u0027s environment at dispatch in ClaudeExecutor); the verbs live under the task and idea command groups in src/Hall9k.Cli (CliCommandTree.cs). Smallest fix to verify: one guard at the CLI entry for the named verbs, keyed on an environment marker the daemon already sets for a dispatched session (or the worktree\\u0027s run record), refusing with a message that names the run and the owner; read-only commands (show, list, status) and the run-scoped commands a session legitimately uses (work, its own run\\u0027s reporting) stay allowed. A task\\u0027s acceptance criteria must not instruct a session to conclude or abandon anything; the closeout owns that. The Windows window (hall9k-51) holds the run log excerpt; ask over the transport. Tests: unit tests over the guard for one refused verb inside a worktree and the same verb outside it; no git or daemon integration test.
